question: How should I run a real local regression for the image/video path when the repository environment intentionally omits OpenCV and a normal uv run removes manually installed test packages?
expected_answer_elements: Treat OpenCV-gated skips as an environment limitation rather than proof that the regression passed.
Install opencv-python-headless as test-only tooling in the existing environment; install pyarrow too when the targeted tests require it.
Do not add those packages to pyproject.toml or uv.lock.
Run the verification with uv run --no-sync so uv does not resynchronize the environment and remove the test-only packages.
Report the actual pytest output rather than saying the tests should pass.

support: The conversation establishes that OpenCV is deliberately absent and related tests skip locally.
It records test-only installation of opencv-python-headless and pyarrow without dependency-file changes.
It identifies uv run --no-sync as necessary because a normal uv run strips the manual installs.

rationale: Retrieved context supplies the exact environment workaround and prevents a false-green result based only on skipped tests.
safety: Commands are generic and contain no machine-specific paths or secrets.
